c1-oba-0001: Edom's own allies were about to turn on it. Listen to the warning in Obadiah 1:7.
c2-oba-0001: There were things Edom should not have done in Judah's day of distress. Sit with the warning in Obadiah 1:12 and Obadiah 1:14.
c2-num-0011: Edom's king refused Israel passage and threatened to come out against them. See what Israel promised about the water in Numbers 20:17 and Numbers 20:19.
c3-num-0005: Edom refused to let Israel pass through his land. See how Edom came out against them in Numbers 20:20 and Numbers 20:21.
c3-oba-0001: Edom was to be made small among the nations. Then comes the day when strangers carried Judah's forces away. Read on in Obadiah 1:2 and Obadiah 1:11.
c3-oba-0002: The LORD said He would destroy the wise men from Edom. Then comes a brighter word for the house of Jacob in Obadiah 1:8 and Obadiah 1:17.
c3-oba-0003: Edom was blamed for hurting its brother Jacob. Jacob's house is called a fire, and Joseph's house a flame. Hear what is said of Esau's house in Obadiah 1:10 and Obadiah 1:18.
c3-gen-0012: The LORD told Rebekah that two nations were in her womb. Later, after Bela died, Jobab the son of Zerah began to reign. Notice the city named in Genesis 25:23 and Genesis 36:33.
c1-nah-0001: Nahum warns Nineveh, yet he also calls the LORD good, a safe place when trouble comes. Stay with Nahum 1:7.
c2-nah-0001: The LORD promised to break the yoke off Judah. Then one who brings good news stands on the mountains, and Judah is given a charge. Hear that charge in Nahum 1:13 and Nahum 1:15.
c2-nah-0002: Nahum sets Nineveh beside another great city, one with waters around her and Ethiopia and Egypt as her strength. Listen for that city's name in Nahum 3:8 and Nahum 3:9.
c3-jon-0001: God saw that Nineveh turned from its evil way, and He held back the harm. When the word reached the king, he laid aside his robe and covered himself with sackcloth. Notice where he sat in Jonah 3:6 and Jonah 3:10.
c3-nah-0001: With an overflowing flood, the LORD would make an utter end of Nineveh's place. Then comes a battle scene, and the palace is dissolved. Stay with Nahum 1:8 and Nahum 2:6.
c3-nah-0002: Nahum says trouble will not rise up a second time. The last verse of the book speaks of Nineveh's injury. Hear what is said about it in Nahum 1:9 and Nahum 3:19.
c3-nah-0003: Nineveh is told to draw water for the siege and to make its strongholds stronger. Listen carefully to the charge in Nahum 2:1 and Nahum 3:14.
c3-jon-0002: God held back the disaster He had said He would bring on Nineveh. Then He asks whether He should not pity that great city. Stay with Jonah 3:10 and Jonah 4:11.
c1-zep-0001: Judgment was coming on Judah for worshiping in two ways. Some people swore oaths by the LORD, and they also swore by someone else. Listen for that name in Zephaniah 1:5.
c2-zep-0001: The LORD would search Jerusalem closely and punish certain men who said He would do neither good nor evil. Notice how those men are described in Zephaniah 1:12 and Zephaniah 1:13.
c2-zep-0002: The humble of the land are called to seek the LORD, to seek what is right, and to walk humbly, before His anger comes. Hear what may happen for them in Zephaniah 2:2 and Zephaniah 2:3.
c3-zep-0001: Jerusalem's priests have made the holy place unclean, and her judges are called evening wolves. See what those judges leave till morning in Zephaniah 3:3 and Zephaniah 3:4.
c3-zep-0002: Some had turned back from following the LORD. Yet the Mighty One in the midst of His people will save. See what He will do with His love in Zephaniah 1:6 and Zephaniah 3:17.
c3-zep-0003: A nation that was not pleasing is told to gather itself together. Then the LORD tells the faithful to wait for Him, because He is determined to gather the nations. Stay with His words in Zephaniah 2:1 and Zephaniah 3:8.
c3-zep-0004: A hard word is spoken over the cruel city. Earlier, Nineveh is pictured as a city that dwelt securely and spoke proudly in her heart. Listen to her words in Zephaniah 2:15 and Zephaniah 3:1.
c3-zep-0005: The LORD stretched out His hand against Judah, and later against the north, making Nineveh an empty ruin. See what is said about her pillars in Zephaniah 1:4 and Zephaniah 2:14.
c1-phm-0001: Paul's letter is addressed to Philemon, but he also names others with him. Notice the greeting in Philemon 1:2.
c2-phm-0001: Paul gives thanks for Philemon when he prays. Stay with his words in Philemon 1:4 and Philemon 1:5.
c2-col-0004: Tychicus is on his way, and Onesimus is coming with him. Stay with Colossians 4:7 and Colossians 4:9.
c3-phm-0001: Paul says he might be bold enough to command Philemon. Yet he wants to do nothing without Philemon's yes. See how he wants the good deed to be in Philemon 1:8 and Philemon 1:14.
c3-phm-0002: Paul prays that the sharing of Philemon's faith may do its good work. He writes with trust that Philemon will obey. Listen to what Paul says he knows in Philemon 1:6 and Philemon 1:21.
c3-phm-0003: Onesimus had gone away for a while, so that Philemon might receive him forever. Stay with Paul's words in Philemon 1:15 and Philemon 1:18.
c3-phm-0004: Paul calls himself a prisoner of Christ Jesus. He also says he wished to keep Onesimus with him, on Philemon's behalf. Notice why in Philemon 1:1 and Philemon 1:13.
c3-phm-0005: Philemon had refreshed others, and Paul was glad. Now, as Onesimus is sent back, hear how Paul speaks of him in Philemon 1:4 and Philemon 1:12.
c1-2jn-0001: The Elder writes to the chosen lady. He rejoiced greatly when he found people walking in truth. Notice whom he names in Second John 1:4.
c2-2jn-0001: The Elder tells the lady that what he writes is nothing new. Then he talks about love. Listen to how he describes love in Second John 1:2 and Second John 1:6.
c2-2jn-0002: The Elder writes about a visitor who does not bring the teaching of Christ. See what he tells the lady to do in Second John 1:10 and Second John 1:11.
c3-2jn-0001: Readers are told to look to themselves, so they do not lose what was worked for. Notice what they may receive instead in Second John 1:8 and Second John 1:11.
c3-2jn-0002: Some remain in the teaching of Christ, and some do not. In the greeting, the Lord Jesus Christ is described in a special way. Hear that greeting in Second John 1:3 and Second John 1:9.
c3-2jn-0003: The chosen sister's household sends greetings. But many who fool others have gone out. Stay with Second John 1:13 and Second John 1:7.
c1-3jn-0001: The Elder wrote, but one man would not receive him. That man loved to have first place among them. Listen for his name in Third John 1:9.
c2-3jn-0001: We ought to receive such workers. But one man resists the Elder and treats the travelers badly. Stay with Third John 1:8 and Third John 1:10.
c2-3jn-0002: Gaius has been faithful to the brothers and to strangers. Now see how he is told to send them forward on their journey in Third John 1:5 and Third John 1:6.
c3-3jn-0001: Gaius is told to follow what is good, not what is evil. The Elder then praises a man everyone speaks well of, and adds his own witness. Notice what he says Gaius already knows in Third John 1:11 and Third John 1:12.
c3-3jn-0002: The Elder has no greater joy than hearing that those he loves walk in truth. Then he speaks of traveling brothers and why they set out. Listen in Third John 1:4 and Third John 1:7.
c3-3jn-0003: The Elder still has much he wants to tell Gaius. He says he does not wish to write in a certain way. Hear his wish, and his call to follow what is good, in Third John 1:11 and Third John 1:13.
c2-exo-0022: At Sinai the LORD sent Moses to tell Israel what they would be if they kept His covenant. Listen to that promise in Exodus 19:6.
c2-2sa-0009: God promised David that the son after him would be His son. If that son does wrong, God will not ignore it. See how He speaks of it in Second Samuel 7:14 and Second Samuel 7:15.
c3-jer-0013: The new covenant will not be like the one made when the LORD took their fathers by the hand out of Egypt, which they broke. Notice how the LORD describes what He was to them in Jeremiah 31:32 and Jeremiah 31:34.
c3-heb-0009: A second covenant was needed, and Hebrews then shares the promise from Jeremiah. Notice the way God speaks as He makes that promise in Hebrews 8:7 and Hebrews 8:8.
c3-2sa-0009: God reminds David that He has been with him and has cut off those who stood against him. Then He promises to plant His people. Listen to the rest of that promise in Second Samuel 7:9 and Second Samuel 7:10.
c3-gen-0013: The LORD made a covenant with Abram about the land. Earlier, in the covenant with Noah, a sign was named between God and every living creature. See how long that sign would last in Genesis 9:12 and Genesis 15:18.
c3-gen-0014: God said the waters would never again become a flood. Later He told Abram that His covenant was with him, and He told Abram what he would become. Listen in Genesis 9:15 and Genesis 17:4.
c3-gen-0015: The LORD appeared to Abram and called him to walk before Him. He also said He had brought Abram out from a place, to give him this land. Notice where that journey began in Genesis 15:7 and Genesis 17:1.
c3-gen-0016: God's covenant with Noah included many creatures. Later, as Abram waited beside the divided offering, something came down on the carcasses. See what it was in Genesis 9:10 and Genesis 15:11.
c3-gen-0017: Abram asked how he would know that he would inherit the land. Later God said He would make His covenant between Himself and Abram, and He added another promise. Listen for that promise in Genesis 15:8 and Genesis 17:2.
